definitions.explanation: A staircase that turns around a central axis as it rises. Found in towers, lighthouses, and narrow buildings where a straight flight would not fit.

examples.japanese: らせん{階段|かいだん}を{上|のぼ}った。
examples.english: I went up the spiral staircase.

examples.japanese: この{店|みせ}は{二階|にかい}へらせん{階段|かいだん}でつながっている。
examples.english: This shop is connected to the second floor by a spiral staircase.

examples.japanese: {灯台|とうだい}のらせん{階段|かいだん}は{急|きゅう}で、{上|うえ}まで{登|のぼ}ると{息|いき}が{切|き}れた。
examples.english: The lighthouse's spiral staircase was steep, and I was out of breath by the time I reached the top.

notes:
らせん (spiral, helix) + {階段|かいだん} (stairs). らせん is normally written in kana; the kanji {螺旋|らせん} appears mostly in older or decorative text.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- らせん{階段|かいだん}を{上|のぼ}る／{下|お}りる: to go up/down a spiral staircase
- {鉄|てつ}のらせん{階段|かいだん}: an iron spiral staircase
- らせん{状|じょう}: spiral-shaped (the same らせん used of anything that coils)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {階段|かいだん}: stairs — the general word
- {回|まわ}り{階段|かいだん}: winding stairs — a stairway that turns, without necessarily coiling around a single post
